questions.question: What is SQL injection and how do you prevent it in Ruby/Rails?
questions.title: SQL Injection Basics
questions.direct_answer: SQL injection happens when untrusted input is concatenated into a SQL string: `User.where("name = '#{params[:name]}'")` lets an attacker pass `'; DROP TABLE users; --` and run arbitrary SQL. Prevent it with PARAMETERIZED queries / placeholders — never interpolate user input. In Rails, `User.where(name: params[:name])` is safe (Active Record binds the value); `User.where("name = ?", params[:name])` is safe too (? is a placeholder). Never use string interpolation (`"...#{params[:x]}"`) or `.to_sql` with user input. The danger: an attacker can read all data, change it, or drop tables. The fix is always the same: keep data separate from code — use bound parameters so the DB treats input as a value, not SQL. Validate input too, but parameterization is the real defense.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know SQL injection is string-concatenated input and that parameterized queries / placeholders prevent it.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Interpolating user input into a SQL string (use placeholders/binders instead).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: SQL injection = concatenating input into SQL. Prevent with parameterized queries (where(name: x) or where("...?", x)). Never interpolate into a SQL string.

sections.title: SQL injection
sections.content:
```ruby
# BAD: string interpolation -> SQL injection
# User.where("name = '#{params[:name]}'")
#   attacker sends:  name = '; DROP TABLE users; --
#   SQL becomes:     name = ''; DROP TABLE users; --'
# User.where("age > #{params[:age]}")              # also bad
# User.find_by_sql("SELECT * WHERE name='#{x}'")   # also bad

# GOOD: parameterized / placeholders (Active Record binds the value)
User.where(name: params[:name])                # hash form (safe)
User.where('name = ?', params[:name])           # ? placeholder (safe)
User.where('name = :n', n: params[:name])       # named placeholder (safe)
User.where('age > ?', params[:age])             # safe

# Why it works: the DB treats the bound value as DATA, not SQL.
# An attacker's  '; DROP TABLE users; --  is just a weird NAME string.

# Raw SQL with user input -> still avoid; if you must, bind:
User.find_by_sql(['SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?', params[:name]])

# Rule: NEVER interpolate/concatenate user input into a SQL string.
# Validate input too, but PARAMETERIZATION is the real defense.
# Keep data separate from code.
```
